messages:
Nadia V: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands runtime section — two asks from product and ops: a one-paragraph blurb for PMs about what "adaptive batching" actually buys customers, and a clear rollback/alert threshold for canary.
Omar H: One-paragraph (draft): Adaptive batching tunes the microbatch window at runtime based on recent sequence-length distribution and queue depth. Benefit: keeps median token latency down by ~8-12% on text-gen while avoiding p95 spikes for skewed long-seq workloads. Opt-in alpha via route config; defaults unchanged.
Priya S: Nice. Ops needs thresholds for automatic rollback in case canary misbehaves — concrete numbers please.
Evan (kernel): Recommend triggers: p95 latency up >7% vs baseline sustained for 20m OR KV cache hit-rate drop >12% absolute. If either fires, runbook: pause traffic, flip kernel fallback, and rollback canary.
Marta L: Can we also add an SLA note for Dedicated customers? They asked about enforced fallbacks.
Omar H: Yes — Dedicated customers get fallback to non-adaptive path by default if p95 >5% at account level; ops will hold rollout per-customer if requested.
Priya S: Product wants an example config snippet and a 2-sentence release note. Can someone paste both?
Evan (kernel): Example route config for alpha:
```json
{"adaptive_batching": true, "batch_window_ms": 10, "adaptive_window_min_ms": 3}
```
Release note (2s): "Alpha: adaptive batching — expected ~8-12% median latency improvement on text-gen. Opt-in only; possible regressions on tiny prompt workloads; SRE rollback thresholds in place."
qa-bot: Created perf job perf/adaptive-canary-297654 with baseline comparison. Results will post to: https://console.redwood/perf/jobs/297654
Marta L: Thanks — I'll update the canary runbook with the alert numbers and add RNW-4120 for per-account fallback policy.
Nadia V: Perfect. Omar/Evan — when you open the docs PR, please paste it here so I can forward to PMs. Closing thread after PR link and perf results.
